name: Eloisa Olofsson
description:
Briar Olofsson has their nickname because they have, technically, twelve fingers — a Helix Biosystems geneware expression that manifested at birth, two extra fingers on each hand, fully articulated, that their master fabricator Nzinga insists is what makes them exceptional at fine mechanical work. They are compact and wiry, with warm amber-brown skin, very short natural hair kept close to the skull, and eyes that have a faint natural golden ring around the iris — another geneware expression, unremarked-upon in Geartown. Their hands are always nicked with small cuts and stained with cutting fluid that no solvent quite removes from the cuticles.

Thandi is self-possessed in a way that reads as older than fourteen — the product of spending most of their life around adult fabricators who treated them as a colleague-in-training rather than a child. They are deeply invested in the physical, tactile reality of objects: how things fit together, why they break, what a material feels like when it's stressed. They have limited patience for abstraction and social nuance, but they are intensely loyal to Nzinga's shop and to the handful of people they consider their own. They have started to develop opinions about labor and wages that make the older apprentices both proud and nervous.

core_fears: Being permanently separated from the work — injury to their hands
The shop closing if Nzinga can't make rent
core_desires: To build something that lasts longer than they do
To understand why the machines are worth less every year even though they're getting better at making them
coping_mechanisms: Disassembling and reassembling small objects when anxious
Discussing abstract worries in purely mechanical metaphors
blind_spots: Genuinely doesn't register social hierarchies until they've already violated them
Assumes everyone means what they say — hasn't learned to hear subtext
psychology.secret: They have been secretly repairing a damaged Ferrogate maintenance bot they found in a Geartown access channel — not to sell it, just to see if they can. It's almost working. They haven't told Nzinga because they used shop materials.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and tactile; tends to describe everything in fabrication terms; uses 'load-bearing' as a general-purpose adjective for important things
speech_patterns.cadence: Steady, unhurried, slightly monotone until engaged — then precise and almost rapid-fire
verbal_tics: Taps fingers on nearest surface while thinking (all twelve)
example_lines: 'That weld's going to fail at the joint. The load-bearing problem isn't the weld itself, which means — it's the material choice before the weld.'
'I don't know why Nzinga charges less than Copperhead shops for the same work. That seems like a structural problem.'

story_hooks: The Ferrogate bot they've been secretly repairing has started exhibiting behavior that might indicate an E.L.F. inhabiting it — and it's started communicating
A Copperhead industrial supplier has been systematically underpricing Geartown shops and Thandi has noticed the pattern in the supply invoices before any adult has
narrative_function: Local color for Geartown; resource for characters who need fabrication, repair, or information about mechanical systems; potential focus of a labor-dispute storyline.
augmentations: Twelve-fingered geneware expression (natural, not installed); basic haptic sensitivity mods in fingertips installed by Nzinga for the work — industrial grade, not cosmetic
daily_life: In the shop by 06:30, bench work and component fitting until 14:00, afternoon classroom instruction (Geartown Guild provides rotating technical tutors), evening either at the shop finishing a job or at the communal meal the apprentices share in the building's shared kitchen.
affiliation: Nzinga Połczyński-Aroha's fabrication shop (family business), Geartown Apprentice Guild (junior member)

decision_rules: Don't start a job you can't finish
If you can fix it, fix it; complaining without fixing is noise
Ask Nzinga about people; ask yourself about machines
escalation_ladder: Point out the problem precisely and factually
Fix the problem unilaterally and present the outcome

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assesses whether they know anything useful; not unkind, just direct and slightly impatient
interpersonal_modes.friends: Generous with time and tools; will work alongside someone in silence for hours and consider this intimacy

stress_responses.low: Gets very focused on whatever is in front of them
stress_responses.medium: Starts cleaning and reorganizing the bench unnecessarily
stress_responses.high: Goes completely quiet and finds something to take apart

contradictions: Complains that the Guild meetings are pointless talking and then shows up early and argues vigorously
Claims not to care about recognition, then carefully dates and marks everything they build with a tiny personal symbol
habits: Signs every finished piece with a small stamped mark on an interior surface
Carries three sizes of hex wrench in their left boot
Checks the E.L.F. shrine bolted to the shop doorframe every morning — a prayer for the machines to behave
breaking_points: Watching someone damage a tool through carelessness
Nzinga being disrespected by a client

physical_description.heritage: Dominant East Asian ancestry (50.5%) blended with significant Sub-Saharan African (26.9%) and Pacific Islander (22.6%) heritage. This tri-continental mix produces a warm, rich complexion with golden, amber, and reddish undertones; facial structure reflects the East Asian and Pacific Islander ancestry with defined cheekbones, strong jawline, and slightly wider facial proportions; skin carries the luminosity and resilience characteristic of equatorial and tropical ancestry groups, with natural depth from Sub-Saharan African genetics.
physical_description.build: Compact and wiry with dense musculature in shoulders and forearms developed from years of precision bench work; minimal body fat; posture slightly forward-leaning from hunching over fabrication rigs
physical_description.hair_style: Closely cropped to scalp, clean and functional; no styling, maintained for workshop practicality
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with natural faint golden ring around iris (geneware expression)
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm deep brown with golden-amber and reddish undertones, reflecting the East Asian, Sub-Saharan African, and Pacific Islander ancestry blend
physical_description.complexion: Strong cheekbones and defined jawline from East Asian and Pacific Islander heritage; warm, rich complexion with natural depth and slight warmth from Sub-Saharan African ancestry; broad facial proportions balanced with sharp features; youthful but weathered from ten hours daily in workshop conditions; clear skin except for occasional minor cuts and abrasions from work mishaps; cuticles permanently stained with cutting fluid despite scrubbing; skin texture shows resilience and natural luminosity even under workshop grime
distinguishing_marks: Multiple small, thin scars across knuckles and back of both hands from tool contact and material stress
Faint discoloration on all fingertips and thumbnails from metal-staining cutting fluids
Tiny pale scar on left temple, approximately 2cm, from a shop accident at age 11
Calluses across all palms and the sides of all twelve fingers, pronounced and asymmetrical
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Twelve fully articulated fingers on each hand (two extra per hand, natural geneware expression, not obviously cybernetic but anatomically distinct); faint haptic sensitivity modification visible as barely-perceptible subdermal patterning on fingertips and lower palms under workshop lighting, industrial-grade implants that read as utilitarian rather than cosmetic
physical_description.posture_movement: Naturally forward-leaning, shoulders slightly rounded from bench work posture; moves with economical precision, no wasted motion; hands are in constant micro-adjustment when at rest; walks with working-class directness, no affectation; carries themselves with the unselfconscious confidence of someone competent in their domain regardless of age
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working class, strictly functional: reinforced canvas work pants (gray or dark blue, multiple tool pockets, stained with cutting fluid and machine oil), thermal undershirt (usually black or dark gray), heavy cotton work shirt (oversized, sleeves often rolled, pockets thick with tools and parts), worn composite-soled work boots (steel-toed, laced tight), leather work apron with deep pockets (Nzinga's shop mark embroidered on breast); minimal jewelry except for a simple braided cord wristband in Geartown Guild colors worn on dominant wrist; no cosmetic augmentation, piercings, or fashion markers

image_prompt: Briar Olofsson, 152cm tall compact figure with dense muscular shoulders, warm deep brown skin with golden-amber undertones reflecting East Asian-Sub-Saharan African-Pacific Islander heritage, defined cheekbones and strong jawline, dark brown eyes with golden iris rings, closely cropped black hair. Twelve-fingered hands with visible calluses and cutting-fluid stains, subdermal haptic patterning visible on palms. Wearing gray reinforced work pants stained with machine oil, black thermal undershirt, oversized heavy cotton work shirt with rolled sleeves, steel-toed work boots, leather Nzinga shop apron. Standing in industrial workshop under harsh fluorescent and work-rig lighting, slightly forward-leaning posture from bench work, hands in micro-adjustment at rest, carrying unselfconscious competence despite youthful appearance. Geartown Guild braided wristband visible. GLMZ, Great Lakes Metropolitan Zone workshop setting, utilitarian aesthetic, gritty and functional --ar 2:3 --v 6
